why_not_recorded: Constructed from llama.cpp's documented API shape, not captured from a live server. The machine this was written on has no weights and no llama-server, so nothing here is a capture and it does not claim to be (CLAUDE.md Guardrail #7). The shape is llama.cpp's own: get_res_model_info returns data[0].meta carrying vocab_type, n_vocab, n_ctx, n_ctx_train, n_embd, n_params, size and ftype. Two of the numbers below are real rather than invented. n_ctx_train is 262144, measured and written up in docs/reference/benchmarks/two-call-window-sizing.md. n_ctx is 49152, which is what config/models/qwen3.5-9b-q4km.json declares. The rest are stand-ins and case 5 reads none of them.
why_not_props: The file is named for the row that created it, and the document inside it is the model list rather than /props, because /props does not carry a trained context length. llama.cpp's get_res_props publishes default_generation_settings, total_slots, model_alias, model_ftype, model_path, modalities, media_marker, the endpoint switches, chat_template, chat_template_caps, bos_token, eos_token, build_info and is_sleeping - and nothing about how long a window the weights were trained for. That number is published on /v1/models and only there, so that is where case 5 reads it.
how_to_record: Start the server as digest.yml does, then: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/models
